facts.statement: Rhoetosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of 9 tonnes.
facts.quote: Rhoetosaurus is estimated to have been about 15 m long, weighing about 9 t.

facts.statement: Heber Longman discovered the first fossils of Rhoetosaurus in 1924 at Durham Downs near Roma in Queensland.
facts.quote: In 1924, Heber Longman, self-trained paleontologist at (and later director of) the Queensland Museum in Brisbane, learned of a large fossil reptile skeleton exposed in the Walloon Coal Measures at Durham Downs near Roma in southern inland Queensland.

facts.statement: The specific name brownei honors Arthur Browne, the station manager who provided the initial fossil fragments to Longman.
facts.quote: The station manager, Arthur Browne, forwarded fragments of bone to Longman, and was honoured with the dinosaur's specific name brownei.

facts.statement: By 2012, the known fossil material included 40 vertebrae, parts of the pelvis, and much of the right hind limb.
facts.quote: By 2012, prepared material comprised 40 vertebrae, five partial thoracic ribs, part of the sacrum, fragments of the ilia, an ischium, the left and right pubic bones, and much of the right hind limb (femur, tibia, fibula, astragalus, and pes).

facts.statement: To date, the tail tip, forelimbs, and skull of Rhoetosaurus have not been found.
facts.quote: Hasta la fecha, el extremo de la cola, los miembros anteriores ni el cráneo se ha encontrado.

facts.statement: Rhoetosaurus lived approximately 162 to 155 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 162 a 155 millones de años durante el Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Australia.

facts.statement: A 2012 study placed Rhoetosaurus as a basal sauropod outside Eusauropoda, though its exact position remains debated, but confirmed it was not a Neosauropod.
facts.quote: In a 2012 phylogenetic study, Rhoetosaurus was found to be a basal sauropod just outside of Eusauropoda, but the authors noted that support for its position was weak, and that its placement as a eusauropodan could not be rejected, but that it definitely was not a member of Neosauropoda.

facts.statement: Longman initially classified Rhoetosaurus as a cetiosaurid based on advice from Friedrich von Huene due to its primitive nature.
facts.quote: Inicialmente Longman, bajo consejo del principal paleontólogo alemán Friedrich von Huene, observando la naturaleza primitiva de Rhoetosaurus y durante mucho tiempo, fue considerado un cetiosáurido.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Rhoetosaurus might have had a clubbed tail due to its supposed relationship with Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: Dado su relación supuesta a Shunosaurus, podría tener una cola terminada en una porra.

facts.statement: The name Rhoetosaurus means "Rhoetus lizard" and refers to a titan from Greek mythology.
facts.quote: Rhoetosaurus (meaning "Rhoetus lizard", after a titan in Greek mythology) is a genus of sauropod dinosaur
